title: Fix: dt-merge-queue accepts local-ci only with a verified Woodpecker target_url
description:

**Why.** Today every `local-ci` status is posted as `chrizefan` with no `target_url`, so a seat-started `twelvex_ci.py` run (twelve-x #368, 03:58/04:11 Rome on 21 Oct) and the Woodpecker cron worker (04:31 Rome) are indistinguishable. Branch protection is unavailable on the private plan, so the queue is the only gate.

**Scope.**
1. The Woodpecker worker (`~/Code/local-ci` worker / `deploy/local-forge/ci/pipeline.yml`) sets `target_url` to its Woodpecker build URL when posting `local-ci`.
2. `dt-merge-queue` verifies the URL shape and the build (read-only Woodpecker API call) before counting `local-ci`.
3. Tests for: missing target_url, wrong host, build sha mismatch, build not success, good case.
4. Note in the PR how the launchd host runner (curren
monitorNotes: PR #6142 at head 4ded7180e5. The merge is the queue's, under the DevOps Lead. title: Fix: dt-merge-queue merges a PR whose latest review verdict is changes requested (a blocking verdict on a stale scope counts as spent)
description:
**Defect.** The merge queue treats a blocking verdict (`changes_requested` / `changes_needed`) as spent once its `scope=@<sha>` commit is no longer the head (any new commit, rebase or merge-from-develop), and then lets `reviewed:agent` satisfy review coverage. **Not covered by digithings#6145 (DIG-4795).** #6145 binds markers to the head and to a different seat, but `_carries_review_evidence` counts any `Review verdict:` line or readable marker as evidence regardless of its value, so a head-bound changes-requested from another seat still passes; and it ships in `shadow` mode. title: call_prefixed_tool sends the substituted, truncated tool name — MCP servers reject namespaced tools (found by DIG-408)
description:
## Pre-existing bug found while carrying the tool allowlist across the HTTP boundary

Found by [DIG-408](/DIG/issues/DIG-408) (leaf 284.1 of [DIG-284](/DIG/issues/DIG-284)). Reported, **not fixed** — `mcp_client.py` is shared code and this leaf's brief scoped it to "report, do not fix".

### The defect

`call_prefixed_tool` reconstructs the remote tool name by **stripping the server prefix off the offered name**, so the remote MCP server is asked for a tool name that **it never advertised**. title: digichat + digigraph: an operator MCP server currently gets an all-or-nothing tool grant and no approval gate
description:
Child of DIG-102. Found while answering the question "can digichat write to the ticket system" — the answer was no, and part of the reason it should stay no for now is this.

**The two holes, with file:line.**

1. **Tool exposure is per-server, not per-tool.** `apply_mcp_extra_tools()` (`digigraph/src/digigraph/tool_policy.py:106-142`) unions *every* tool name discovered on an operator MCP server into the turn's allowlist. The only filters are the user's disabled tokens and the `web_search` shape check. There is no per-tool allowlist for MCP-proxied tools. So attaching a server hands the model everything that server lists, read and write alike.
2. **There is no approval step anywhere.** A search of digigraph and digichat for a tool-approval, human-in-the-loop, or confirmation gate returns nothing. Tool calls execute on the model's decision inside `max_tool_rounds=4`. Every write is unattended.

Today the platform survives this by pointing every operator MCP server at something read-only — `scripts/zammad_mcp` (GET only, pinned by `tests/scripts/test_zammad_mcp.py::test_server_registers_read_only_tools`) and DataTap's `mcp+search`-scoped dev MCP. That is defence by the choice of ser

title: VPN WireGuard rotation review - strict router causing outages
description:
## Problem
The VPN rotation system (vpn-rotate) caused a major outage:
- Locked on a single VPN location that was rate limited
- Blocked ALL agents from running (rate limited on one country)
- VPN router runs in background, cannot be overridden
- Prevented opening OpenCode sessions on terminal

## User Feedback
"The VPN router is causing more harm. It is very strict and runs in the background and I cannot override it. It was even forcing me where I could not open any open code sessions even on my terminal. So we need to relax it a bit. I am not sure how we would do that. Maybe give me a way out if I want to turn it off. Because it runs and it executes in the background. It is my entire laptop. We need to do a review about the VPN wire guard."

## Required Changes
1. **Add override/disable mechanism** - User needs a way to disable VPN rotation when it causes problems
2. **Review WireGuard config** - Current setup may be too aggressive
3. **Add rate-limit detection** - Should detect when current VPN country is rate limited and auto-rotate
4. **Add manual control** - CLI flag or env var to disable/enable rotation

title: IT: Board alert on recovery-observability when resolution counters stay at zero
description:
Build item 4 from DIG-1648.

**Problem:** `GET /api/companies/{companyId}/recovery-observability` shows `alert.breached: true` for two consecutive weeks (2026-09-28: 3.1%, 2026-10-05: 190%). **Every resolution counter is 0** — `resolvedTakeovers: 0`, `handedBack: 0`, `ownerCompleted: 0`, `otherTakeover: 0`, `selfRecovery: 0`. This has been invisible to the board.

**Current state:** The endpoint returns `alert.breached` but no notification is sent. A threshold breached for two weeks reaching nobody is not a monitor.

**Fix needed:** Add a board alert/notification when:
- `alert.breached: true` AND
- `handoff.resolvedTakeovers + handoff.handedBack + handoff.ownerCompleted + handoff.otherTakeover + handoff.selfRecovery === 0` for the latest week
- This condition persists for >1 week

**Alert channel:** Board wake / board inbox / dedicated IT channel

**Verification:** When recovery rate exceeds threshold AND all resolution paths are dead, the board receives an alert within 24 hours.

**Parent:** DIG-1648
**Priority:** Highest — this is how 16,805 board-owned actions went unnoticed.

title: deploy-digithings-stack-cloudflare.yml has no push:main trigger, so merges to main never deploy, and nothing alerts on a pending production gate
description:
## The production deploy workflow does not deploy on merge

`.github/workflows/deploy-digithings-stack-cloudflare.yml` triggers on **`pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` only**. There is no `push: main` trigger.

Consequence: **merging to main deploys nothing.** A fix can be reviewed, approved, squash-merged into main, and still never reach production.

### How this caused a live customer-data exposure

On DIG-1484 we removed a committed seed payload containing unmasked customer PII from `apps/digithings-stack-cloudflare/container/seed/occ_tickets.jsonl` (blob `91669454da41ef3af7f7e7a115f96dce8dd1808f`, 1,518,223 bytes, 919 chunks). The payload was removed from the tree at 2026-10-06 02:25Z.

The retirement of that payload, plus a `SHARED_STACK_CONTAINER_ID` bump from `shared-v16` to `shared-v17`, was merged correctly as `da88fa71` at 19:06:58Z on 2026-10-06. Production served `shared-v16` for roughly **19 hours after the code fix existed in main**.

Verified live during this incident:

```
curl -sf https://graph.digithings.ai/_stack/meta   ->  containerId = shared-v16
```

The deployment that would have carried the fix sat in the `production` environment gate waiting for a human

title: local-ci: the swap gate false-trips on macOS dynamic swap and a skip posts a sticky failure, so 12+ PRs into develop are blocked
description:
Board watch 02:15 CEST 15 Oct. Found while tracing the DIG-3083 burn-down (Repo CI tick 00:17Z: all 12 BLOCKED PRs fail only on `local-ci skipped: swap free 735MB < 900MB`).

Evidence (`~/.config/digithings/logs/local-ci/local-ci.log`): local-ci has skipped every tick since 01:17 CEST (about 23:17Z), with swap free 727-855MB against `MIN_SWAP_MB = 900`. At the same time `memory_pressure` reports **81% system-wide memory free**. `vm.swapusage` free is headroom inside the swap files macOS has already allocated (total 4096M). macOS adds swap files on demand, so a low `free` value does not mean the Mac can't run checks.

Second bug, in the uncommitted `local_ci.py` working copy (DIG-3660 must-fix 5): when skipping, it posts `failure` ("local-ci skipped: ...") on up to 2 pending PRs per tick. `pending()` then drops any PR that already has a `local-ci` status (`has_status`), so a skipped PR is **never re-checked** when the gate clears. It stays red until someone re-pushes or runs `--pr N` by hand. The blocked list grows by 2 every tick while the gate is tripped.

1. Gate on real memory pressure (for example `sysctl kern.memorystatus_l

title: digichat: system prompt and tool traces leak into client-visible output
description:
Found in client mail during intake on 2026-10-04. Filed from [DIG-94](/DIG/issues/DIG-94).

Our own client contact tested the prototype against a competitor and called the result "utterly disqualifying in front of a paying customer".

- 11 of 100 test answers showed the system instruction. One showed it 181 times.
- The teaser email the client received on 2026-09-30 contains raw "1 tool call", "5 tool calls" traces and the meta question "Would you like me to escalate any of these tickets".

**Fix:** no system instruction may appear in a client-visible answer. Tool traces and internal meta questions must leave the answer body; if a trace is useful it belongs in a collapsed details view. Add a test that fails when a system instruction leaks.

Use the codename `occ-prototype`. Do not name the client company. Full detail is in the first comment.

title: digichat: the OCC prototype answers without a tenant header and returns digithings internal data
description:
Found in client mail during intake on 2026-10-04. Filed from [DIG-94](/DIG/issues/DIG-94).

The API was called with **no OCC tenant header** and returned digithings' own internal showcase document, which says OCC "may later embed under `/chat/occ` as a separate tenant surface; that is out of scope for this showcase and not part of the current digithings.ai/chat product".

Two failures: there is no tenant isolation, and an internal digithings document is reachable from the client surface.

**Why it is more than a bug:** the client asked three questions on 2026-08-23 and we have answered none. Is the OCC instance in production? What is its service level and rate limit? **Where does the data sit?** The last one matters, this is sold on GDPR grounds.

**Fix:** fail closed, no tenant header means no answer. Confirm the data region and retention and write it down. Use the codename `occ-prototype`. Full detail is in the first comment.

title: Server must reject unauthenticated writes to /api/issues (401, not 201)
description:
## An unauthenticated write to `/api/issues*` returns 201 and is filed as Chris

Parent: [DIG-1254](/DIG/issues/DIG-1254). Root cause proved there by probe; this leaf is the server-side fix.

### The defect, reproduced

```
POST /api/issues/25a16d95-116c-4df5-a78d-a241d904cbdf/comments
(no Authorization header)
→ HTTP 201
→ { "authorType": "user", "authorUserId": "local-board",
    "authorAgentId": null, "onBehalfOfUserId": null,
    "createdByRunId": null, "metadata": null }
```

A write with **no credential at all** is accepted and permanently attributed to the board user. The server does not refuse it. That is the entire bug.

For contrast, with `Authorization: Bearer $PAPERCLIP_API_KEY` the same request returns 201 with `authorType: "agent"`, `authorAgentId` set and `createdByRunId` set — so **server-side attribution logic is already correct**. Do not go looking for an attribution bug. There is none.

The anti-spoofing guard also already exists: a body `onBehalfOfUserId` is refused with 422 *"Responsible user cannot be chosen by the caller (Server-derived attribution)."* That guard works and should be left alone.

### Why it matters

Every writer that loses or misuses its crede

title: Repair remaining multi-issue worktree bindings in digithings
description:

122 execution workspaces are bound to 2+ issues. That is what corrupted

## What to run, per issue, two calls

```
PATCH /api/issues/{id} {"executionWorkspacePreference":"isolated_workspace"}
PATCH /api/issues/{id} {"executionWorkspaceId":null}
```

Both are confirmed working as CTO. After them the issue reads
`pref=isolated_workspace, ws=null` and the next run provisions a fresh worktree off develop.

## Rate limit — the reason this is a separate issue

The API enforces a **per-run cross-issue write budget of 20 writes**:

```
429 This run has spent its cross-issue write budget (Per-run cross-issue cap of 20 writes).
```

Each issue costs 2 writes, so one heartbeat repairs 10 issues. 841 issues need roughly 85 runs.
Batch across runs; do not retry inside one run.

## Order

1. Closed issues first (`done`/`cancelled`). Zero runtime risk. 426 of them.
2. Then open issues not checked out and not locked.

title: Fix: validate DT_DIGIGRAPH_PORT as a plain integer port before templating the digigraph health-check URL (#6153 follow-up, DIG-4797)
description:
Follow-up to DIG-4797 / digithings#6153 (merged to develop 21 Oct 12:06 Rome, merge commit `24fd0b9f85`, head `58ca2943dd`). Note: #6153 merged on head `58ca2943dd` while its last approve named `4358aed8bc`, so the final commit was never reviewed; this ticket closes the security gap QA found in that diff.

**Defect.** `scripts/localstack/contracts.py` templates the digigraph probe as `url="http://127.0.0.1:${DT_DIGIGRAPH_PORT:-8000}/healthz"` and `_expand_env()` substitutes the raw process-environment value. The code comment claims "a value that is not a port makes the URL unparseable rather than pointing it somewhere else" — that is false: `DT_DIGIGRAPH_PORT=8000@evil.com` yields `http://127.0.0.1:8000@evil.com/healthz`, a valid URL whose host is `evil.com` (`127.0.0.1:8000` becomes userinfo). Other shapes do the same (`8000/@evil.com`, `8000#`, `80 00`, `+80`, `0x1F40`, unicode digits). The loopback-only guarantee that `test_builtin_urls_are_labelled_local_loopback` relies on is therefore bypassable through the environment.

**Asks.**
1. Validate `DT_DIGIGRAPH_PORT` before expansion: ASCII digits only (`^[0-9]{1,5}$`, no sign, no whitespace, no unicode digits), integer value 1–65

title: Art. 9 filter on the ingestion path — the measure that gates the next client dataset

**But the finding that matters operationally is not the DPIA. It is Article 9.**

The digithings-cron Worker job `digiquant-house-run-watch` (`apps/digithings-cron/src/house-run-watch.ts`, cron `23 * * * *` UTC) files a GitHub issue on digithings-ai/digithings every hour while the run is missing. title: Paperclip adapter marks recovered ECONNRESET runs as failed (88% false positive)
description:
Route from DIG-2056 (IT lead routing call). The ECONNRESET false-failure is a **Paperclip runtime** defect, not a digithings-repo defect. Confirmed at source in `~/paperclip-fixes/pcsrc-8f8a0ab` @ `dd777f4b`, and verified live against the installed `@paperclipai/adapter-opencode-local` 2026.1001.0.

## The defect

`packages/adapters/opencode-local/src/server/parse.ts:88-103` accumulates **every** `error` frame seen anywhere in the JSONL stream into `errors[]`, then reports:

```ts
errorMessage: errors.length > 0 ? errors.join("
") : null,
```

There is no notion of whether the run continued after the error. `parseOpenCodeJsonl` is a stream reducer, but the fatal/non-fatal distinction it is being asked to make is a property of the **stream as a whole**, not of any single frame.

`packages/adapters/opencode-local/src/server/execute.ts:736-748` (`toResult`) then promotes that stale text into a failure:

```ts
const parsedError = typeof attempt.parsed.errorMessage === "string" ? attempt.parsed.errorMessage.trim() : "";
const synthesizedExitCode = parsedError && (rawExitCode ?? 0) === 0 ? 1 : rawExitCode;
...
errorMessage: (synthesizedExitCode ?? 0) === 0 ? null : fallbackErrorMessage,

title: Fix the js/polynomial-redos alert 196 on format-json-dump.ts: real quadratic whitespace strip
description:
Owner: Security Engineer. Due 2026-10-28. CodeQL alert 196 (js/polynomial-redos, severity high) is open on develop since 2026-10-21. Not stale: alert 195 was dismissed as a false positive today, this one was not.

Where: packages/ui/src/components/chat/gallery-thread/format-json-dump.ts L75, inside repairPartialJson():
  out = out.replace(/\s+$/, "");
Reached for every tool argument or result whose text fails JSON.parse: tool-fallback.aui.tsx L251-278 -> JsonView -> formatJsonDump -> repairPartialJson. Nothing caps that input length.

Fix (lane S): out.replace(/\s+$/, "") -> out.trimEnd() (linear, same semantics), and cap the input length before repair.

Acceptance: a linear-time test with 50000 mid-string spaces asserts under 500 ms and unchanged content; input length capped before repair; CodeQL re-analysis on develop closes alert 196.

Evidence (Node): s = '{"a":' + ' '.repeat(n) + 'tru}' puts the whitespace mid-string so the anchor never matches: quadratic. n=2000 2.8 ms, 4000 6.2, 8000 27.7, 16000 115.2, 32000 470.8, 64000 1910.5 ms. Same string with trailing whitespace: 0.1 ms. A 1 MB whitespace run blocks the main thread for minutes.

title: Fix: exit-0 runs recorded as cancelled, and recovery re-blocks issues the run set to in_review/done (heartbeat finalizer, paperclip fork)
description:
**HOLD-NEW-WORK note:** this is allowed clearing work (it stops finished tickets from being re-blocked; it unblocks the drain). Approved by One 2026-10-21 09:18 Rome as a PR in the digithings-ai/paperclip fork only.

## Problem (Board diagnosis, 2026-10-21)
Runs that end cleanly (exit code 0, adapter finished, work done) are recorded as **cancelled** with:
- run event `lifecycle` "run cancelled", payload `cancellation: {reason: "Execution stopped without a recorded cancellation request", source: "unknown", expected: false, initiator: {type: "system"}}`
- no `POST /heartbeat-runs/:id/cancel` exists in `service.log` for these runs (checked), so nobody asked for the cancel.

Recovery then logs "Automatic recovery stopped. Recorded work is preserved; actions with unverified outcomes will not be repeated." with `cause: legacy_execution_requires_reconciliation`, `replay: blocked`, `automaticRecovery: preserve_without_replay_v1`, and writes `issue.execution_recovery_settled {replay: not_authorized, outcome: blocked}`. That **moves the ticket to `blocked` even when the run itself had just set it to `in_review` or `done`**.

title: DIG-50 leaf A: anchor placeholder patterns in the credential guard
description:
**Lane: S** · leaf of [DIG-50](/DIG/issues/DIG-50) · base branch `feat/50-credential-guard-shape` · commit under test `3fd5b306d`

Read this whole brief before touching anything. You are not exploring; the files and line numbers below are the work.

## Goal

One behavior: `is_placeholder()` must stop classifying a value as a placeholder when the placeholder word appears **anywhere inside it**.

A placeholder marker counts only when it sits at the **start** of the value (separator-tolerant), or when the whole value is an angle-bracket template, or when the value is empty.

Today `PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS` is matched with an unanchored `re.search`, case-insensitively. So `your_`, `example_`, `test_`, `dummy_`, `placeholder`, `changeme` and `<.*>` all match as substrings anywhere. A real credential long enough to satisfy the value-shape patterns is waved through whenever it happens to contain one of those words in the middle.

title: Decide whether to rotate the three credentials scrubbed by PR #5030 - they remain valid in git history
description:

PR #5030 (merged to `develop` as `ed210dc4c`) scrubbed three committed credential values out of

title: Stop new issues being created with reuse_existing: enforce isolation at creation
description:
Follow-up to [DIG-1635](/DIG/issues/DIG-1635). That sweep repairs instances of the defect. This fixes the **inflow**, so new issues stop arriving broken.

## The headline

The repair rate is an order of magnitude below the inflow. **This sweep cannot reach zero.**

```
repair rate, one heartbeat                          10 issues
new issues/day landing on an already-shared ws      ~95
legacy backlog (140 shared workspaces)             1,256 issue slots
```

Sweeping all 1,256 slots would take ~126 heartbeats, and the number would not be zero when it arrived.

## The leak is still open, and DIG-1619's setting works

DIG-1619 set `executionWorkspacePreference` to `isolated_workspace`. Measured over all 1,876 issues:

```
pref=isolated_workspace  -> no-ws           30    <- never shares a workspace
pref=null                -> no-ws          163
pref=reuse_existing      -> SHARED-ws      269    <- all of the damage
pref=reuse_existing      -> unique-ws      148
```

`isolated_workspace` never shares. Not once. But DIG-1619 closed at 2026-10-06T21:20:05Z and **307 issues were created after it. 203 are `reuse_existing`; 133 already sit on a workspace another issue holds.**

title: local_ci.py: an explicit --pr N run must evaluate a closed or merged PR
description:
Context: DIG-4776 (parent), finding 2 of the night of 2026-10-20.

Bug: local_ci.py only ever looks at OPEN pull requests. list_prs(base) runs `gh pr list -R REPO --base base --state open --limit 200 --json number,headRefOid,...`, and main()'s explicit `--pr N` path iterates only that open list. So an explicitly named PR that was closed or merged before the run is silently never evaluated: the run reports nothing and looks like it did the work. That is exactly what happened to #6087, which other session automation closed mid-flight: the local-ci run for it evaluated nothing and nobody noticed until the deploy lane broke again.

Task: in ~/Code/local-ci (its own git repo), make the explicit-PR path resolve the PR whatever its state, so `--pr N` on a closed or merged PR still produces a verdict (and a clear "PR is closed/merged" outcome) instead of a silent skip. Add a test in test_local_ci.py covering the closed-PR case.

title: Paperclip API starvation: heartbeat scheduler detoasts a 55 KB context_snapshot per row
description:
2026-10-21, during the DIG-4738 status-card run, the local Paperclip API starved for roughly 25 minutes: every /api/* route hung (connection accepted, no response, >150 s) while / and /health answered 200 in about 10 ms. No Paperclip restart was performed (hard ban) and no credential file was read.

DIAGNOSIS

The node server (pid 67863, 127.0.0.1:3100) has an 11-connection pool. All 11 connections were busy on IO-bound SELECTs issued by the heartbeat scheduler:

- heartbeat_runs: 27,550 rows, heap 49 MB but TOAST 2,568 MB. Each row stores a whole context_snapshot of about 55 KB in TOAST. The scheduler query `select "agent_id","created_at", context_snapshot->>'issueId', context_snapshot->>'taskId' from heartbeat_runs where company_id=$1 and agent_id in (33 ids) and created_at > $35` has to detoast every candidate row just to extract two keys: about 19,000 buffer reads, 25 s on its own, minutes under concurrency. The planner cannot see TOAST cost, so it keeps choosing the heap path.
- heartbeat_run_events: 365,000 rows, heap 149 MB, TOAST 1,210 MB. The family query `select distinct on (run_id) ... where message like 'Bounded retry exhausted%'` does a full 149 MB sequential scan.

title: Architect: decide stranded routine_execution policy - re-drive or block (DIG-2120 Defect B)
description:
Child of DIG-2120. **Decision needed, not a code task.** Platform analysed Defect B and stopped, because the obvious fix is a trap. Evidence and options in `/Users/chrisstefan/paperclip-fixes/dig-2120/DEFECT-B.md`.

## The trap

`findLiveExecutionIssue()` (`routines.js:1208`) uses `innerJoin(heartbeatRuns, ...)` in both branches, filtered to `LIVE_HEARTBEAT_RUN_STATUSES` (`:22`). An inner join cannot return a row with no matching run, so a stranded execution issue (`executionRunId` null, no live run) is invisible to the concurrency gate, and `skip_if_active` never fires. That is the reported defect.

**Swapping `innerJoin` -> `leftJoin` makes it worse.** The result feeds the policy at `:1463`: `if (activeIssue && concurrencyPolicy !== "always_enqueue")` -> `skipped`. Make stranded executions visible and `skip_if_active` treats them as **active**, so the routine skips **forever**. A routine that never fires again is worse than one that fires into the void: it reads as "cadence healthy, nothing to do".

A stranded execution is not an *active* execution, it is a **broken** one. The gate has no vocabulary for that state, and adding one is the actual work.

description:

title: IT: Truthful blocked/blockedBy combination for recovery actions
description:
Build item 3 from DIG-1648.

**Problem:** DIG-534 shows `status: blocked` but `blockedBy: []` (zero blockers). The blocker is a recovery action, not another issue. The current state is unreadable from the board.

**Fix options (pick one):**
1. **Extend `blockedBy` to reference recovery actions** — allow `blockedBy` to include recovery action IDs, so `blockedBy: ["recovery:bd45c805-961b-44f1-b9f7-26cfcb573de3"]` makes the dependency visible.

description:

Consequence: when a later sweep re-selects a desk id band that straddles a dead day's publications and stamps the digest with its own run day (the 7 Aug NY / 19 Aug NY / 20 Aug / 18, 21, 22 Sep cases), it is **impossible after the fact to prove which release date any individual stored file carried**. This was limitation L1 in the DIG-551 answer and it is not recoverable retroactively — only prospectively fixable.

Change: log the release date (and source release-date field) alongside `file_id` on each store line, and persist it as a column so the digest builder can group by research date rather than run date if that is ever wanted.

title: Promote fixes on develop, not only on main: a main-only fix is reverted by the next promotion

The promotion that landed the 2.6.2 line at 23:47Z reverted them again, and the lane was broken when it ran.

**A price observation dated after the run date must fail closed, with its own code `future_anchor`.**

```python
ANCHOR_FUTURE_GRACE_DAYS = 1   # declared next to ANCHOR_MAX_AGE_DAYS

# appended LAST in anchor_unusable_reason, after the existing four:
if (fix.as_of - ref).days > ANCHOR_FUTURE_GRACE_DAYS:

```

Three constraints on how this lands, all from the ruling:

A price 30 days in the future means a query-bound bug, a timezone bug, or a bad source, and you look at none of those. title: [owner: IT Lead] vpn-rotate cannot rotate: three locks pin every config to US-MA-217.conf, so the DIG-1538 acceptance criterion is unreachable
description:
## Problem

DIG-1538's acceptance criterion is `vpn-rotate next` rotates between different countries. That is impossible today even if every config download succeeds, because **three independent locks are each pinned to the single path `US-MA-217.conf`**:

1. **Application guard.** `tools/vpn-rotate` `up(st, name)`:
   ```python
   if name != "US-MA-217":
       sys.exit(f"Error: Only US-MA-217 is allowed. Config '{name}' is not permitted (DIG-1564).")
   ```
   The same guard is repeated in `cmd_use`. So `next` will pick a country and then refuse it.
2. **The sudoers rule** names the literal path `/Users/chrisstefan/.config/vpn-rotate/configs/US-MA-217.conf` twice (up and down).
3. **The wrapper** `/usr/local/bin/vpn-rotate-wg-quick` validates that the config resolves exactly to `US-MA-217.conf`.

This was deliberate. `it/vpn-rotation-review.md` line 14 records why: the account was locked on a single VPN location, US-MA-217, because of rate limiting. Pinning was correct when there was one config. It is now the thing standing in the way of DIG-1538.

I verified (1) by reading the shipped code. I could not read (2) or (3) directly - they are root-owned and `sudo -n` needs a password

description:

The live OCC tenant registry (digichat worker, Workers KV key embed-tenants) nevertheless carries a models section: a default plus an available list of six house model ids with allowPicker true. The current apply path on the DIG-4488 branch writes only the legacy secret, so the KV write is the missing piece. Counsel's target state, the code proof and the two traps are on DIG-4750 and on DIG-4488. title: feed-confirm watchdog reads a blocked run as healthy: evaluateFeedConfirm never reads run conclusion
description:
## Definition of done

`evaluateFeedConfirm` raises an alarm when a confirm run exists in the lookback window but none concluded `success`, and the test suite covers `completed` + `failure`.

## The defect

`apps/digithings-cron/src/twelvex-watch.ts` line 183-195. `evaluateFeedConfirm` filters on `r.status === "completed"` and never reads `r.conclusion`.

GitHub reports a **billing-blocked** run as `status=completed, conclusion=failure`. The run object completes while no job ever starts. So the watchdog reads a blocked run as a healthy completed run and returns `alarm: false`.

`evaluateCatchup` in the same file already does it correctly (`r.conclusion === "success"`). The feed watchdog does not.

## Proof

twelve-x `feed_published_confirm.yml` runs:

    2026-10-14T14:41:11Z  completed  success
    2026-10-14T14:41:21Z  completed  success
    2026-10-15T14:41:51Z  completed  failure   <- billing block, DIG-4379
    2026-10-15T14:41:57Z  completed  failure   <- billing block, DIG-4379
    2026-10-16T14:41:52Z  completed  failure   <- billing block, DIG-4379
    2026-10-16T14:41:57Z  completed  failure   <- billing block, DIG-4379

All four failures satisfy `status === "completed"`.

title: Stop operator-prompt secrets from resolving under the production keychain prefix
description:
Fix scripts/dt-secrets so a local secret render never falls through to the production keychain prefix.

Root cause: keychain_prefixes() (scripts/dt-secrets:261-270) returns the DT_SECRETS_KEYCHAIN_PREFIX override and then the contract prefix "digithings/" (config/contract/secrets.yaml:29). from_stores() (182-196) tries every prefix in order. The operator-prompt branch of resolve() (273-308) calls from_stores(name, prefixes, allow_prompt=False), so a value absent under "digithings-local/" resolves from production and the operator is never asked. dt up renders with --no-prompt (scripts/localstack/orchestrate.py plan_up), so it binds a production credential.

Affected entries, all source operator-prompt: DIGICLAW_DIGIKEY_API_KEY (secrets.yaml:192), DIGIGRAPH_UPSTREAM_API_KEY (:202), DIGISEARCH_SEED_API_KEY (:282), E2E_BEARER_TOKEN (:292).

Fix: split the prefixes into local and shared. operator-prompt reads only the local prefixes (the DT_SECRETS_KEYCHAIN_PREFIX override and a new contract key local_keychain_service_prefix: "digithings-local/"), then prompts, and reports missing under --no-prompt. source keychain keeps reading local plus shared. Failing test first. Full brief in comme

title: Drop an expired trial proof and ask the tenant page to re-mint it
description:
Deliverable: the embed client drops a proof the server reported as expired, and asks the tenant page for a fresh one over the existing postMessage channel. The proof stays in memory only, and the client never presents a proof it has dropped.

Why this leaf exists (Frontend Engineer, comment f5c65c9a on DIG-769, 2026-10-20T03:16:07Z, and the Code Reviewer's class review on DIG-769): the proof is a 10-minute bearer, the page relays it once, the client presents it on every request and never checks its age. So after ten minutes the client still sends a dead proof. "The server must answer a stale proof with a signal that says expired. Then the client can drop the proof and ask the page to re-mint it. Without that signal the client cannot drop it safely." This leaf is the client half; the server half is a sibling leaf owned by Backend Engineer, Reliability.

CONTRACT (fixed by EM, cross-leaf - do not invent another shape):
- The server signal is the RESPONSE HEADER `x-embed-trial-proof-expired: 1` (see the server sibling leaf). The client reads it on the chat response.
- The client's request to the page is a postMessage to the same parent window the `trial:proof` message arrives on, with

title: fix(ci): repair the review-coverage gate query (StatusCheckRollup has no nodes field)
description:
The review-coverage gate cannot read check results. PR #6029 changed the query, but the new form is also wrong.

GitHub's GraphQL type StatusCheckRollup has no nodes field. The field is contexts(first: N) { nodes { ... } }. The query in the gate script asks for statusCheckRollup { nodes { ... } } at lines 261-268. GitHub answers undefinedField, fieldName nodes, typeName StatusCheckRollup. The parser at line 452 reads rollup.get("nodes"), so state["checks"] is always empty.

Effect: two of the five coverage arms can never fire. Arm 1 needs a successful Bugbot check. Arm 3 needs a successful CodeRabbit or Claude code-review check. A commit whose only review evidence is a bot check is then reported as not reviewed, and the gate still prints that all commits were reviewed. The gate run also prints about 1300 error lines and hides them.

This is not a new breakage. Before #6029 the query used statusCheckRollup { contexts { ... } }, which GitHub also rejects, because the fragments must sit inside contexts { nodes { ... } }. The arms were dead before and after, so the promotion of PR #5995 is not made worse by this. #6029 is a no-op that claims to be a fix, and its commit message gives a

title: fix(chat): re-add the ReasoningTrigger import - packages/ui no longer compiles (DIG-4653)
